newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada, sales union suspend talks.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada, sales union suspend talks.

text.p: The union representing 3,500 Air Canada customer sales and service and direct marketing agents said on Monday that talks with the airline were suspended on Saturday, September 28 after four weeks of negotiations on a new contract.
A leadership meeting will take place this week in Toronto prior to strike votes commencing on October 3, 1996, Canadian Auto Workers Local 2213 said in a statement.
Following the conciliation process, members will be in a legal strike position in time for Christmas, it said. The current collective agreement expires at midnight today.

"Air Canada has refused to address our members' issues," said Cheryl Kryzaniwsky, president CAW Local 2213. "We leave the table without even having received an economic offer from Air Canada, only rhetoric about the company's continued need for concessions."
